summary: OptimaCorp's travel and expense policy note promotes a per diem system, a fixed daily allowance for lodging and meals, in place of traditional actual-expense reimbursement. It argues that per diems cut paperwork, give employees autonomy, speed up the finance team's work, and are fair because rates track destination costs. It also cites environmental benefits from fewer paper receipts and frames the policy as an expression of trust in employees.
one_line: OptimaCorp replaces actual-expense reimbursement for lodging and meals with fixed daily per diems, citing less admin, employee autonomy, fairness and lower paper use.
key_facts: OptimaCorp's travel and expense policy introduces per diems for accommodation and meal expenses.
A per diem is defined in the note as a fixed daily allowance for lodging and meals.
OptimaCorp says per diems are far superior to the traditional actual expense reimbursement model.
Per diems remove the need to save receipts, fill out complex expense reports, and wait for reimbursement approvals.
Employees decide how and where to spend their per diem budget, including where to eat and stay.
The finance team can close the books faster because it does not have to review countless receipts.
Per diem rates are determined based on the cost of living and average prices in the destination.
OptimaCorp adjusts per diems for expensive cities to suit the destination's living costs.
If a conference provides meals, the per diem for that day is adjusted accordingly.
OptimaCorp claims per diems avoid the discrepancy or inequality that often comes with actual expense reimbursements, so nobody is out of pocket for doing their job.
Per diems support OptimaCorp's environmental commitment by reducing paper use and promoting a digital approach.
The policy states the company values accountability, transparency, and simplicity, and offers an open-door policy for questions.
